solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Legume that makes you smart, hot

parts.note: chic means smart or stylish, and it is what makes you look so
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A pulse that leaves your mouth stinging, it is so spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' reads as stinging pain beside 'hot', but it means stylish here. CHICH is an old name for the chickpea.
explanation.definitionFit: The chich or chickpea is a pulse plant, a member of the pea family grown for its seeds.

clue.text: Tapered longs for madam, unusually scant pair with soft lining (10, two words)

indicators.note: with soft lining means having the soft letter placed inside
unusually means in an unexpected way, so the letters fall in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
p, piano, means soft in music

explanation.surface: A woman's slim long trousers made from a skimpy pair with a soft lining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Longs' is a noun here, as in long trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri pants are close-fitting women's trousers tapering to mid-calf.

clue.text: Lake runs into Tasmanian river

indicators.note: into means going inside, so one part is placed within the other

parts.note: the Huon is a river in southern Tasmania
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A lake drains into a river in Tasmania.
explanation.definitionFit: Huron is one of the five Great Lakes of North America.

clue.text: Misread quiz — every other to be written out in form of Arabic

indicators.text: every other to be written out
indicators.note: writing out every other letter leaves only the alternate ones that remain

parts.note: the second, fourth and every following other letter

explanation.surface: A quiz read wrongly, half its letters to be copied into Arabic script.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraqi Arabic is the dialect spoken in Iraq, a regional variety of the language.

clue.text: Former errand boy half caught up in casualty

parts.note: cad once meant an errand boy or odd-job man

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
half means only part is kept and the rest is dropped

parts.note: taken as written; its first half is kept

explanation.surface: An old messenger boy, partly caught up in an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casualty' is an injured person to the surface, but here it is the old sense: a chance event or windfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Caduac is an old Scots word for a casualty in the sense of a windfall or chance happening.

clue.text: Cross feline, best avoided?

parts.note: a cat is a feline
tabu, a variant of taboo, describes what is best avoided

explanation.surface: An angry cat that you would do well to steer clear of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as an adjective for the cat, but it is a noun: a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattabu is a hybrid bred from domestic cattle and the zebu, so it is a cross.

clue.text: Off-key cornist controls only one function

definitions.note: a description of what the thing does, standing for the noun

indicators.note: off-key means out of tune, so the letters are out of order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An out-of-tune horn player is limited to a single role.
explanation.walkthrough: A cornist is a horn player.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistron is a stretch of DNA coding for a single polypeptide, so it governs one function.

clue.text: Penetrating wound in outer parts of ankle

indicators.note: in puts the first item inside the second

parts.note: ankle's first letter
ankle's last letter
a cut is a wound

explanation.surface: A deep wound on the outside of the ankle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outer parts of ankle' supplies both its first and last letters, A and E, around the wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Acute and penetrating are synonyms for sharp, as of a mind or a pain.

clue.text: Part of sponge from set in washing trough

indicators.note: in puts the first item inside the second

parts.note: a tye is a trough for washing ore in mining
a lot is a set of items, as at an auction

explanation.surface: A piece of a bath sponge, retrieved from a sink.
explanation.definitionFit: A tylote is a needle-like spicule with knobbed ends forming part of a sponge's skeleton.

clue.text: Impact poorly where love's involved — there's no sex in its production

definitions.text: there's no sex in its production

indicators.note: poorly means badly done, so the letters are put in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Things go badly when love gets mixed up in it, and then nobody sleeps together.
explanation.definitionFit: An apomict is a plant reproducing by apomixis, setting seed without fertilisation, so asexually.

clue.text: Fiasco damaged oar in current down under

parts.note: a bomb is a flop or disaster, especially of a show

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rowing disaster: a broken oar in an Australian rip.
explanation.walkthrough: Down under means Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombora is an Aboriginal-derived Australian word for dangerous broken water over a submerged reef.

clue.text: Icelandic money, gold, cut thin

indicators.note: a word that is cut has lost a piece, here its final letter

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
rare means thin, as rarefied air is

explanation.surface: Iceland's currency, made of gold but sliced very fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurar is the plural of eyrir, a hundredth of the Icelandic króna, so it is a unit of that money.

clue.text: One given company housing … poky, ill-fitting, unpleasant (7, two words)

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: housing means giving a home to, so one part sits inside another

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: something ill-fitting does not sit in its proper shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shown into a cramped, badly fitted room finds it nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis is surface punctuation only. Icky-poo is a jokey, babyish extension of icky.
explanation.definitionFit: Icky-poo is a childish colloquial intensive of icky, meaning nasty or distasteful.

clue.text: Gallery in favour of accepting a bit of promotion

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: pro means in favour of
an advertisement is a piece of promotion

explanation.surface: A gallery welcoming some publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prado in Madrid is one of the world's great art galleries, so it is an example.

clue.text: Proceed with difficulty, as tiro in AZ challenge?

indicators.note: in places the learner inside the challenge's word

parts.note: the monthly Azed clue-writing competition, a comp for short
a tiro is a beginner, and L is the learner plate

explanation.surface: A beginner struggles along in an Azed clue-writing contest.
explanation.walkthrough: AZ is Azed himself, whose clue-writing competition accompanies the plain puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: To clomp is to walk heavily and clumsily, so it means to move along with effort.

clue.text: Spurn a line at sea, dealing with old land campaign

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A naval commander refuses one route afloat while running a war on land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' and 'land' set up a naval picture; 'at sea' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Peninsular War was Wellington's land campaign in Spain and Portugal against Napoleon, so peninsular relates to it.

clue.text: Peeled potato cakes, part of salade verte?

indicators.note: peeling takes off the skin, so the outer letters go

parts.note: croquettes are fried cakes of mashed potato

explanation.surface: Skinned potato cakes served as part of a French green salad.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the first and last letters leaves ROQUETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Roquette is rocket, a peppery leaf often included in a French green salad.

clue.text: Something produced by TV chef, say, vaguely anoretic

definitions.text: Something produced by TV chef, say

indicators.note: something put vaguely is not in a fixed form, so the letters are loosely reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A television cook's dish that seems somewhat lacking in appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: A creation is anything made or invented, and a chef's latest dish is commonly called one.

clue.text: Old clown, log splitting head

indicators.note: splitting means driving through the middle, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
a chock is a block or log of wood

explanation.surface: A clown of old cleaving a skull with a log.
explanation.walkthrough: Pate is a dated or jocular word for the head, especially its crown; patchocke itself is Spenser's coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchocke is a Spenserian word for a boor or clown, now obsolete.

clue.text: Rodent I found under a bed

indicators.note: in a down entry, under means placed below, so that letter comes after the rest

parts.note: taken as written
a couch is a bed or sofa
taken as written; under places it below in a down entry

explanation.surface: A rodent discovered beneath a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The acouchi is a small South American rodent related to the agouti.

clue.text: Monkey mum kept in train, disciplined

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so one part sits within the other
disciplined means drilled into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A monkey is held aboard a train and punished by its mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarin is a small South American monkey related to the marmoset.

clue.text: What's leech at messing about in e.g. haemoglobin?

definitions.text: What's leech at messing about in e.g. haemoglobin?

indicators.note: messing about means fiddling around, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: What is a bloodsucker doing, fiddling with someone's blood?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a leech feeds on haemoglobin-rich blood, and haemoglobin contains a chelate.
explanation.definitionFit: A chelate is a compound where a metal atom is gripped by a ring-forming molecule, as iron is in haem.

clue.text: E.g. Boater in Blanket, name for a cocktail

indicators.note: in puts the first item inside the second

parts.note: a manta is a Spanish blanket or wrap
a boater is a kind of straw hat
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone names a cocktail after a straw hat wrapped in a blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manhattan is a cocktail of whisky and sweet vermouth, named after the New York borough.

clue.text: 'Hoy' precedes this dam fool

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
a nana is a silly person

explanation.surface: An exclamation followed by a foolish mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoy is Spanish for today, which comes before tomorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Mañana is Spanish for tomorrow, the day that comes after today.

clue.text: Ornamental monogram that's horrible in pictures put up

indicators.note: in puts the first item inside the second
in a down entry, put up means the letters run upward

parts.note: pictures are art
ugh is the cry at something horrible

explanation.surface: A decorative monogram that looks awful hung up in a gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tughra is the elaborate calligraphic signature of an Ottoman sultan, a decorative monogram.

clue.text: Talk idly about high honour — it affects nothing (8, two words)

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the chatter goes round the honour

parts.note: to natter is to chat idly
the Order of Merit, a high British honour

explanation.surface: Chatting about a grand award makes no difference.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a sentence of its own: saying no matter is saying it is of no consequence.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase signals that something is unimportant and changes nothing, so it fits a statement of no effect.

clue.text: Crack marksman historically not left in charge regarding aim?

indicators.note: not means without, so one letter is removed

parts.note: William Tell, the legendary Swiss archer
L for left, the letter dropped
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A sharpshooter of legend, no longer in command, concerned with his target.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun on aim, Tell's skill and also purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Telic means directed towards an end or purpose, so concerning an aim.

clue.text: Tense travelling? Lost footing

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
on the road means travelling, so the road stands for it

explanation.surface: Nervous on a journey, someone has slipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost' means obsolete: Spenser's troad meant a path or footing.
explanation.definitionFit: Troad is an obsolete form of trod, meaning a track or footing, hence a lost word for it.

clue.text: Ornamental tile, part of mantel lady erected

indicators.note: in a down entry, erected means set upright, so read from the bottom
part of means only a section of the following words is used

parts.note: the letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A decorative tile on the mantelpiece that a woman put up.
explanation.definitionFit: A dalle is a decorative flagstone or tile, from the French for slab.

clue.text: Graf duel disfigured — did it distinguish him at the front?

definitions.text: did it distinguish him at the front?

indicators.note: something disfigured has lost its proper shape, so the letters are mangled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A German count scarred in a duel: was that his mark of distinction at the front?
explanation.walkthrough: Graf is German for count, and duelling scars once marked German officers; the definition instead points to his uniform's colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Feldgrau, field grey, was the colour of German army uniforms, which identified a German soldier at the front.

clue.text: Thin sod, hard to read, led away

indicators.note: led away means the letter for 'led' is taken out and removed

parts.note: a scrawl is untidy, illegible writing
L, read as 'el', and led sounds alike; it is the letter removed

explanation.surface: A skinny person, hard to understand, was escorted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thin sod' looks like an insult to a person; it is a thin piece of turf.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraw is an Irish word for a thin turf or sod, used for roofing.

clue.text: Accompaniment for curry, hot, swallowed by airhead?

indicators.note: swallowed by means taken inside, so the first item sits within the second

parts.note: a doll is slang for a pretty but empty-headed person
H for hot

explanation.surface: A brainless type gulping down something spicy beside a curry.
explanation.definitionFit: Dholl, or dal, is a lentil dish served alongside curry in Indian meals.

clue.text: Commando, no gent certainly, holding rear

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside, so one part is placed within the other

parts.note: cit, short for citizen, was a scornful term for a townsman, no gentleman
hind means rear, as in hind legs

explanation.surface: A rough soldier, hardly a gentleman, guarding the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chindits were a British special force fighting behind Japanese lines in Burma, so a Chindit was a commando.

clue.text: Burden, extra-large? Offload some packing

indicators.note: unloading the packing around something leaves only what sits in the middle

parts.note: the letters remaining once the outer packing is shed

explanation.surface: An oversized load: time to unload some of the wrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burden' looks like a load; it is a song's refrain, its burden.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden is the refrain of a song, and tra-la is a meaningless sung refrain.

clue.text: Loan intended to include closure thereof

indicators.note: to include means taking something in, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: your intended is the person you are engaged to
thereof points back to the clue's first word, loan, whose last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A loan meant to cover its own repayment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closure thereof' is the closing letter of 'Loan' itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To finance something is to provide the money for it, which a loan does; both work as noun and verb.

clue.text: Leggy bird? Got 'er measure by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is judged by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: to weigh her is to get her measure

explanation.surface: A long-legged woman being sized up by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the two sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A wader is a long-legged bird such as a heron, which feeds by walking in shallow water.
